extracted.intended_audience: general readers, journalists, media organizations, researchers interested in media policy and disinformation
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts the stated aims, practices, scope, and legal/operational constraints described for the Trusted News Initiative (TNI) — an international alliance of news media, social media and technology companies focused on countering disinformation. The page covers TNI's formation, scope (topics of focus), methods (tools, early warning, education, conferences), membership, regional expansion, and legal controversies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of disinformation to be targeted
rubrics_metrics.description: The Trusted News Initiative (TNI) is an international alliance ... working to identify and combat purported disinformation about national elections, the COVID-19 pandemic and COVID-19 vaccines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page repeatedly identifies elections and public-health topics (COVID-19 and vaccines) as primary subject-matter priorities for TNI activity and coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rapid, collective action to undermine disinformation
rubrics_metrics.description: Launch plans to develop tools to assist industry partners in 'moving quickly and collectively to undermine disinformation before it can take hold.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes speed and coordinated responses across partners as an operational standard for effectiveness; implies prioritizing early intervention rather than slow, isolated responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop and use tools and systems (e.g., Early Warning System)
rubrics_metrics.description: This led to the launch of a 'Trusted News Charter' ... Other projects were to include an online media education campaign ... Early Warning System set up to combat fake news during U.S. Presidential Election.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TNI intends to build technical and organizational tools (including Early Warning Systems) that enable partners to detect and respond to misinformation campaigns; examples include collaboration with Project Origin and other technology-led efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public education and voter information dissemination
rubrics_metrics.description: Other projects were to include an online media education campaign and disseminating information on how to vote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities aimed at educating the public and providing authoritative civic information are part of TNI's strategy, not just content moderation or takedowns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipation and preparedness for election-related misinformation
rubrics_metrics.description: It continued to engage in information management related to elections, announcing in July 2020 that it was anticipating misinformation campaigns in advance of the 2020 United States presidential election.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactive anticipation of campaigns is highlighted as a criterion for readiness and planning, rather than purely reactive measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-stakeholder collaboration among news media, social platforms and tech firms
rubrics_metrics.description: TNI is an international alliance of news media, social media and technology corporations which claim to be working to identify and combat purported disinformation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Membership and joint activity across traditional news organizations, platforms (Facebook/Meta, Twitter/X, YouTube), and tech companies (Google, Microsoft) are presented as a core operational design principle for legitimacy and reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional expansion and partner training
rubrics_metrics.description: The TNI announced its expansion into the Asia-Pacific region in November 2022, providing new partners from the area with training in navigating disinformation with funding from the Google News Initiative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TNI measures success partly by geographic reach and capacity-building (training) for regional partners, often with external funding support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge-sharing via conferences and webinars
rubrics_metrics.description: Trust in News conferences (TIN21, TIN22, TIN23) featured webinars on 'how to tackle disinformation' led by representatives of TNI members; topics have included Ukraine, climate change, AI, and Big Tech's role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular conferences and publicly documented webinars are used as mechanisms for disseminating best practices, coordinating approaches, and focusing attention on topical threats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement with provenance and verification projects (e.g., Project Origin)
rubrics_metrics.description: TNI Director Jessica Cecil highlighted the work of the TNI and the related Project Origin, led by Microsoft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation in provenance/verification projects is cited as part of the initiative's toolkit for validating media and combatting manipulated content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on source threat attribution (foreign adversaries) and domestic audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Cecil suggested that institutional efforts to counter disinformation should focus on foreign adversaries such as Russia and China, as well as domestic consumers of disinformation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TNI's strategic emphasis includes both attributing/disrupting state-linked campaigns and addressing the information needs/behavior of domestic audiences affected by disinformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and legal constraints (antitrust and public-records considerations)
rubrics_metrics.description: An antitrust lawsuit alleges collusion to censor individuals and news outlets; the Information Commissioner's Office ruled that communications between the BBC and members of the TNI were not subject to public disclosure under the Freedom of Information Act 2000. The U.S. DOJ filed a statement urging courts to find that colluding to suppress competing viewpoints can violate federal antitrust law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TNI's practices are framed against legal constraints: coordination must be mindful of antitrust risks and public-transparency rules; these legal considerations shape acceptable collaboration and information-sharing practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership breadth as a legitimacy signal
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants and members include major international and national news agencies, broadcasters, and platforms (AFP, AP, BBC, Google, Microsoft, Reuters, Facebook/Meta, Twitter, NYT, WSJ, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wide and diverse membership across reputable outlets and platforms is presented as part of the initiative's claim to authority and capacity to influence the information ecosystem.
